I do apologize for the double post.  


Hi MSstats team

I am trying to use MSstatsTMT for analyzing TMT10 data that I obtained from Maxquant search. Here are few questions: 

1- Is there anyway that you can share the "MQ_Annotation.csv" file? I didn't find it in the GitHub page. I would like to use it as template to generate my own MQ annotation file for TMT experiments. 

2- I have done 2 sets of TMT10 for 18 individual samples (3 conditions X 6 replicates). I have also pooled all samples, labeled (131), and ran one channel in each TMTsets for the pooled sample. In other words, each TMT10 set has 9 individual samples + 1 pooled sample. I was hoping to use the pooled sample intensity values to normalize and remove potential batch effects between two sets of TMT10 experiments. 

I have seen a similar approach in this paper called iRS normalization: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28325852

Is there anyways to implement this in MSstatsTMT?

I hope my questions make sense. 

HFaz

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT questions
parts:
Hi HFza,

Thank you for being interested in MSstatsTMT. We have submitted MSstatsTMT to Bioconductor. You can directly install MSstatsTMT from Bioconductor after Nov. 1st https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/html/MSstatsTMT.html.

For your questions,

1. Attached is the "MQ_Annotation.csv” file: 
  • Run: MS run ID. It should be the same as Raw.file info in evidence.txt.
  • Channel : Labeling information (channel.0, ..., channel.9). The channel index should be consistent with the channel columns in evidence.txt. 
  • Condition: Condition (ex. Healthy, Cancer, Time0). If the sample is pooled sample, then the “Condition” column should be “Norm”.
  • Mixture: Mixture of samples with different TMT reagents, which can be analyzed in a single mass spectrometry experiment. The mixture may be fractionated into multiple fractions to increase the analytical depth. Then one mixture should correspond to multuple MS runs (One fraction is one MS run). For example, if ’Run’ = 1, 2, 3 are three fractions of one TMT mixture of biological samples, then they should have same ’Mixture’ value. In your case, you have two mixtures (two TMT10 sets).
  • BioReplicate: Unique ID for biological subject
2. MSstatsTMT indeed provides similar normalization like iRS. Instead of equalizing the mean of normalization channels (iRS), MSstatsTMT equalizes the median of of normalization channels. When you run the function proteinSummarization(), which performs protein quantification and between-run normalization, set the argument normalization=TRUE to do the normalization you want.

Best,
Ting

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT questions
parts:
Currently MSstatsTMT doesn't have a special treatment for the empty channel. I would recommend you to remove the empty channel column from evidence file before running MSstatsTMT. In the annotation file, only put the 9 non-empty channels.

-Ting

Hi Msstats Team,
I am processing MaxQuant TMT10 output with MSstatsTMT. I would like to know if there is a way to have "gene name" instead of  "protein ID" when processing the data with MSstatsTMT? 
Thanks
HFaz

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT questions
parts:
Hi HFaz,

Current MSstatsTMT doesn't support gene names as protein names for the MaxQuant output. But we have put this suggestion in our future work calendar. 

As a temporary solution, I have revised the MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat() function to support gene names and attached the function code. Now you can read in the "MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2.R" script, call function MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2() to do preprocessing, and then run MSstatsTMT to do the following analysis. 

Here is an example:

library(MSstatsTMT)
source("MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2.R")

input.mq <- MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2(evidence = evidence,
                                    proteinGroups = proteinGroups, 
                                    annotation = annotation.mq,
                                    which.proteinid = 'Gene.names')
head(input.mq)


Best,
Ting
